summary: Completed full production-readiness audit of the GospelDrop Next.js 14 app. Found 8 critical gaps (broken Stripe webhook → no donations recorded, TypeScript errors suppressed, isAdmin/role schema mismatch, wrong sendFulfillmentEmail call signature, no DB migrations, no CI/CD, no deployment config, no README), 11 important improvements, and 8 nice-to-have items. Audit report written to docs/production-readiness-audit.md and a PR opened.
commandsRun: find . -type f | grep -v node_modules | grep -v .git | sort
git commit -m 'docs: production readiness audit report'
knownIssues: No tests were run against the application itself — the audit is static code review only. The app has no CI to run tests against. Tests that do exist (admin-api.test.ts) only test hardcoded data structures, not real application code.

TypeScript compiler (tsc) was unavailable (npx not installed in audit sandbox), so TypeScript errors were identified by reading code and cross-referencing type signatures manually rather than via compiler output.
nextStep: The highest-priority next step is implementing the missing Stripe webhook handler (src/app/api/stripe/webhook/route.ts) since without it no donations are ever recorded and the entire application is non-functional end-to-end. After that, remove ignoreBuildErrors/ignoreDuringBuilds from next.config.mjs and fix the resulting TypeScript errors.
